incidents.description: Mid-workflow session crash lost gemini_validations[], agents_invoked[], and token_budget.dispatches[] arrays for the E1 dispatch. Work was complete in git (afae373) but state was untracked.
incidents.recovery: Retroactive Gemini validation dispatched (gv_20260520_e1_retroactive). Validation read actual files directly and returned 100% PASS. State reconstructed in chore commit c7ab9c5.
incidents.root_cause: Claude Code session termination between agent completion and state-write step. No atomic commit of state + session.
incidents.first_detectable_signal: No gemini_validations entry for E1 task_id in state after crash — detectable immediately on session resume.
incidents.escape_route: State should be written atomically with each agent completion, not deferred to end of dispatch loop.
early_warning_candidates: Check gemini_validations[] count vs completed_tasks[] count on session resume

incidents.description: Code Hardener first scan (06204c2f) scanned wrong codebase. repositoryUrl was set to host-side path (file://~/Code/conductor-dev) which is not reachable inside the Docker container. Scanner silently used stale /scan-target contents from a previous project.
incidents.recovery: Changed repositoryUrl to file:///host-code/conductor-dev (container-side mount path). Re-scan 6912c8c2 produced the correct 12-finding result.
incidents.root_cause: conduct skill prose does not document the container/host path distinction. No error was surfaced; the scanner silently used its fallback target.
incidents.first_detectable_signal: Score was implausibly high (implied near-perfect on new code). A score sanity check against expected-finding-range for new bash code would have caught this earlier.
incidents.escape_route: conduct skill Prerequisites should state: 'For local repos, repositoryUrl MUST use container-side mount path file:///host-code/<dirname> not host path.'
early_warning_candidates: Warn when Code Hardener score on first scan of new code is >950 with no open findings

incidents.description: Gemini-CLI (agy) is wrong shape for one-shot adversarial review. Three attempts all failed — agy is a multi-step agent-mode CLI (Google Antigravity), not a one-shot completion CLI. Adversarial review ran in single-reviewer degraded mode.
incidents.recovery: Documented structural incompatibility. Proceeded with Claude-only review, all HIGH findings fixed. PASS WITH NOTES verdict.
incidents.root_cause: conduct skill adversarial review section assumes a Gemini CLI that accepts a prompt and returns a completion. agy spawns exploration sub-tasks instead.
incidents.first_detectable_signal: agy --help output would have shown the multi-step agent shape before wasting 28+ minutes on a hung process.
incidents.escape_route: Install google/gemini-cli (official one-shot CLI) or wire conductor-kernel:gemini-validator as second reviewer. Add CLI shape-check to Prerequisites.
early_warning_candidates: Before adversarial review, run: gemini --version or agy --version and check for 'completion' vs 'agent' in output

options: Split into 4 separate STANDARD-tier workflows (one per phase)
Bundle all 6 enhancements into one MAJOR-tier workflow
decisions.choice: Bundle all 6 in one MAJOR workflow
decisions.rationale: Dependency graph is linear (E6→E1, E6→E4, E2→E1); splitting would require cross-workflow state handoff. One workflow preserves state coherence.
decisions.reversibility: low — tier re-classification cascades to all gate modes
decisions.outcome: Delivered successfully. Cost: $21.94. Risk signal: tight coupling meant any single enhancement failure could have blocked all six. In practice no enhancements failed.

decisions.reversibility: medium — operator applied diffs manually; region markers can be stripped
decisions.outcome: PASS. Region boundary protection implemented and QA-verified.

what_worked.pattern: Inline fix on PARTIAL validation verdict
what_worked.mechanism: When Gemini returned PARTIAL (91% E6, 71% E3), the specific gap was actionable (missing denylist pattern, awk extraction bug). Orchestrator fixed inline and Gemini re-validated same dispatch rather than triggering full re-dispatch.
what_worked.evidence: gv_20260520_e6 PARTIAL→PASS, E3 PARTIAL_71_then_PASS. Zero re_dispatches_triggered despite 2 PARTIALs.
what_worked.conditions: Requires PARTIAL findings to be specific and contained to 1-2 items. Works when orchestrator can verify the fix directly.

what_worked.pattern: Retroactive Gemini validation for crash recovery
what_worked.mechanism: Treat the delivered git artifacts as the ground truth. Dispatch gemini-validator with the commit + file list instead of re-running the agent.
what_worked.evidence: gv_20260520_e1_retroactive: 100% PASS, all 10 ACs verified from actual file content.
what_worked.conditions: Requires identifiable commit boundary. Not a substitute for live validation — only appropriate when work is demonstrably complete in git.

what_worked.pattern: CISO HIGH findings remediated inline by orchestrator at Phase 1
what_worked.mechanism: CISO-001 (denylist pattern gap) and CISO-002 (audit-emit fail-closed) were catch-and-fix inline during CISO review, not sent back as builder re-dispatch. This saved one full re-dispatch cycle.
what_worked.evidence: CISO verdict PASS_WITH_CONDITIONS (not FAIL). Phase 1 did not require a CISO re-dispatch.
what_worked.conditions: Inline fixes are safe when the fix is additive (add missing patterns) and does not require redesign.

what_worked.pattern: Explicit numbered AC list in QA dispatch prompt
what_worked.mechanism: Dispatching QA with an explicit numbered AC list (AC-E1-1 through AC-E1-10) produced structured PASS/FAIL per-AC verdicts, enabling fast triage of the two E1-7/8 SKIPs.
what_worked.evidence: E1 QA: 8/8 testable ACs PASS + 2 SKIP clearly identified with dependency note. E4 QA: 8/8 ACs PASS.
what_worked.conditions: Most effective when QA is dispatched with the exact AC list from the spec, not a custom test plan.

what_worked.pattern: P1→P4 dependency-ordered phasing for multi-enhancement bundle
what_worked.mechanism: Foundation (E6+E4) shipped before Loop Closure (E1) which depends on E6's change-log. Progressive Disclosure (E2) shipped before E1 which mines the skill index.
what_worked.evidence: No blocking cross-enhancement dependency issues during implementation. E1's AC-E1-7/8 correctly SKIPPED pending E6 live integration (expected deferred dependency, not a bug).
what_worked.conditions: Requires explicit dependency graph in the spec (docs/plans/hermes-sequencing.md was the source of truth).

what_failed.pattern: grep -cF | echo 0 idiom for marker count
what_failed.description: grep -cF exits non-zero when no matches found. Piping to echo 0 via || produces '0\n0' (both grep output and fallback). The [[ $var -ne 1 ]] arithmetic test then errors but does NOT abort under set -euo pipefail — it silently returns false, causing mn_check_markers to return 0 (success) on corrupted markers.
what_failed.proposed_mitigation: Use count=$(grep -cF -- pattern file 2>/dev/null); count=${count:-0} assignment form instead of pipeline. Add to shell scripting rules in process_knowledge.

what_failed.pattern: PostToolUse hot path with multiple jq invocations
what_failed.description: change-tracker.sh ran 5 separate jq invocations to build the change-log entry. Measured 14ms wall time vs 3ms for collapsed single @tsv call. On a busy session with 100 Write/Edit calls per hour: 11ms/call * 100 = ~1.1 sec/hour lost to jq fan-out.
what_failed.proposed_mitigation: Collapsed to single jq --arg ... --argjson ... @tsv call in fix commit e26fdb1. Pattern: always batch jq field extractions into one call on hot paths.

what_failed.pattern: GNU coreutils timeout assumed on macOS
what_failed.frequency: one-off — but would affect all macOS users of change-tracker.sh
what_failed.description: timeout 0.08 sqlite3 ... depends on GNU coreutils timeout command. macOS ships BSD tools; timeout is not present unless coreutils is installed via Homebrew. Result: trigger classification in change-tracker was silently dead on all macOS hosts.
what_failed.proposed_mitigation: Use sqlite3 -cmd '.timeout 80' (built-in SQLite timeout mechanism, no external dependency). Add to process_knowledge/rules: 'never use GNU timeout in cross-platform bash; use tool-native timeout mechanisms.'

what_failed.pattern: E2 QA test plan deviation from spec ACs
what_failed.description: E2 QA was dispatched with 'write a test plan' rather than 'test against these specific ACs.' QA constructed a custom plan with different ACs, producing two false FAILs that were not spec violations.
what_failed.proposed_mitigation: QA dispatch prompts should always include the verbatim AC list from the spec. Consider adding an AC-injection template to the QA dispatch pattern.

what_failed.description: Four errors found: (1) wrong codehardener path, (2) API root /api/ vs /api/v1/, (3) missing redis port collision documentation, (4) wrong Skill tool parameter shape in conductor.md Skill Disclosure Protocol. None blocked this workflow but each would cause confusion for the next operator.
what_failed.proposed_mitigation: File a dedicated MINOR-tier workflow to audit and fix conduct.md Prerequisites block + skill prose errors. All four are surgical edits.

process_knowledge_candidates.title: Never use grep -cF pipeline for marker presence checks
process_knowledge_candidates.rule: grep -cF exits 1 on no-match. Pipeline to || echo 0 produces multi-line output that breaks arithmetic tests. Use: count=$(grep -cF -- 'MARKER' file 2>/dev/null || true); count=${count:-0}
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements adversarial-review HIGH#1, 6 sites, fixed in e26fdb1

process_knowledge_candidates.title: Batch jq field extractions on hot paths
process_knowledge_candidates.rule: PostToolUse and other high-frequency bash scripts must not invoke jq more than once per execution. Use jq --arg / --argjson with @tsv or @json output to extract all fields in a single call.
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements adversarial-review HIGH#2, 5→1 jq call, 14ms→3ms, fixed in e26fdb1

process_knowledge_candidates.title: Use tool-native timeout mechanisms instead of GNU timeout
process_knowledge_candidates.rule: timeout(1) is GNU coreutils and absent on stock macOS. For SQLite: sqlite3 -cmd '.timeout NNN'. For curl: curl --max-time N. For network calls: tool's own --timeout flag.
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements adversarial-review HIGH#3, change-tracker.sh:281, fixed in e26fdb1

process_knowledge_candidates.title: stat is not portable — detect BSD vs GNU form
process_knowledge_candidates.rule: stat -f%z is BSD-only (macOS). stat -c%s is GNU-only (Linux). Use: file_size=$(stat -f%z file 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s file 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements adversarial-review LOW#8, change-tracker-helpers.sh:354, fixed in e26fdb1

process_knowledge_candidates.title: QA dispatch must include verbatim AC list from spec
process_knowledge_candidates.sop: When dispatching conductor-qa, include the exact numbered AC list from the enhancement spec. Do not ask QA to 'write a test plan' without anchoring to specific ACs. Prevents QA from generating a plan that diverges from spec ACs and producing false FAILs.
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements E2 QA CONDITIONAL PASS 6/8 — FAILs were plan-vs-spec divergence, not spec violations

process_knowledge_candidates.title: Code Hardener local scan: use container-side repositoryUrl
process_knowledge_candidates.sop: For local repo scans: repositoryUrl must be file:///host-code/<repo-dirname> (container mount path). Host path file:///Users/... is not reachable inside the Docker container and causes silent fallback to stale /scan-target. Validate by checking that findingsCount > 0 on new code — implausibly clean first scans indicate wrong target.
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements INC-002, scan 06204c2f misfire, corrected in 6912c8c2

process_knowledge_candidates.title: Verify Gemini CLI shape before adversarial review dispatch
process_knowledge_candidates.sop: Before attempting Gemini-based adversarial review: run 'gemini --version' or 'agy --version' and confirm the tool accepts a prompt and returns a completion (not a multi-step agent). agy (Google Antigravity) is agent-mode and will hang or produce narration without findings. Preferred alternative: gemini-cli (google/gemini-cli) for one-shot mode, or wire conductor-kernel:gemini-validator as second reviewer.

process_knowledge_candidates.title: Session crash between agent completion and state write
process_knowledge_candidates.edge_case: If a session crashes after an agent completes work (commit exists in git) but before state arrays are updated, use retroactive validation: dispatch gemini-validator with the commit + actual output files as evidence. Record with retroactive:true in gemini_validations[]. Create a chore() commit to close the phase with reconstructed arrays. Do NOT re-run the agent.
process_knowledge_candidates.evidence: hermes-inspired-enhancements INC-001, E1 crash recovery, gv_20260520_e1_retroactive
